source.title: Body Weight training - the 2 hand Hip Drop - fundamental getup movement for martial artists
quotes: think about this as a time under tension exercise usually what we do is we set up a timer let's say 30 seconds and you would see how many reps you can do in that amount of time
your numbers are going to be low like 8 to 12
the breath pattern is exhale every time the hip bone touches the ground

sourceFacts: A 30-second timed alternating hip-drop example is described; it is one whole bout, not 30 seconds on each side.
8–12 early repetitions and 30 touches in 30 seconds are descriptive examples, not mandatory progression targets.
Quiet step-step transitions, hip/thigh contact and exhale on each hip touch remain the reviewed instruction.
appDecisions: Separate opt-in hipDropTimed profile; default rep-based ground profile and historical policy keys remain unchanged.
Two to four whole 30-second bouts, 60-second rests and the existing configurable clean-exposure gate are app volume/progression choices.
Record actual activity seconds and positive actual touches on both sides; balanced alternating counts may differ by at most one, with either side leading.
No touch-speed quota, automatic timer credit, added load or automatic timed upgrade of the single-hand variation.
Use existing readiness, recovery, re-entry, pain, correction/undo, time-budget and offline-draft contracts.
qualifications: This integrates the bounded 30-second example, not a complete bodyweight 101 program or a universal timing ladder.
Source timing and app-selected sets/rest/progression remain separately identified.
